# Cris Santos Company | Dams | Sole Proprietorship: Dam safety consultant

> Cris Santos Company is a one-person business: Cris Santos owns and runs it alone as a sole proprietorship, operating as a dam safety consultant.

This folder is a self-contained scenario. Read this page first, then open the project folders in step order (step-01 to step-10). Each project folder has a `_context.md` explaining what that deliverable looks like for this company.

> **Completed sample.** All 10 deliverables in this folder are filled in. The detailed company facts they share (locations, systems, current security posture) are in [00_company-facts.md](00_company-facts.md). Read it second.

> **Industry note:** At this size, Cris Santos Company works in the Dams vertical as a dam safety engineering consultant (NAICS 541330) instead of the vertical's primary industry (NAICS 221111). Reason: A sole proprietor cannot operate a hydroelectric dam. Some sector rules may reach it only through customer contracts (flow-down). Confirming that is part of P03.

## What the business handles (typical for this industry)
- **Sensitive data:** CEII (dam inundation maps, design data; 18 CFR 388.113); Vulnerability/Security Assessments and Security Plans; PCII; BES Cyber System Information (for BES hydro)
- **Critical systems:** Spillway and gate control PLCs; Hydro unit control/governor systems; SCADA and remote control centers for multiple projects; Dam safety instrumentation and early-warning systems; Levee pump station controls

This sample's own systems and data are in [00_company-facts.md](00_company-facts.md). Items above that the company does not have are out of scope.

## Who regulates it
SRMA: Department of Homeland Security (CISA); FERC Division of Dam Safety and Inspections (non-federal hydropower licensees); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (federal dams/levees); Bureau of Reclamation (federal dams); NERC (hydro generators meeting BES criteria)

| Requirement | Citation | Size thresholds / exemptions |
|---|---|---|
| [FERC Security Program for Hydropower Projects (Revision 3A)](https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/security.pdf) | FERC D2SI Security Program for Hydropower Projects, Rev. 3A (Mar. 30, 2016), applied to licensees/exemptees under 18 CFR Part 12 and license conditions | Security Group 1/2/3 by consequence, vulnerability and likelihood (DAMSVR); Group 1 and 2 dams carry full VA/SA and security plan obligations; Group 3 lighter; group criteria not public. |
| [FERC dam safety incident reporting](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-18/section-12.10) | 18 CFR 12.10 | None. |
| [NERC CIP Reliability Standards (CIP-002 through CIP-014; CIP-015 approved)](https://www.nerc.com/standards/reliability-standards/cip) | Federal Power Act sec. 215 (16 U.S.C. 824o); 18 CFR Part 40; NERC CIP-002-5.1a, CIP-003-9, CIP-004 to CIP-014 (current enforceable versions) | Impact rating via CIP-002 Attachment 1 bright-line criteria, e.g., medium impact for generation with net Real Power capability >= 1,500 MW in a single Interconnection; high impact for control centers of BA/GOP/TOP controlling >= 3,000 MW; UFLS/UVLS programs of 300 MW or more bring Distribution Providers into scope. Low-impact assets have reduced (CIP-003) requirements. |

Whether each requirement applies at this size is decided at the start of P03, the gap analysis (build step 5).
